pixel_art_reasoning.readability_at_native_scale: A 16x16 status glyph is read at 1x in the full cell and at 3x (48x48) in the enlarged panel. A 1-pixel stroke check tends to read as a thin tick or noise at 1x on a dark panel; the fixture's 3-pixel horizontal runs give roughly 2 px perpendicular weight, which survives 1x and becomes a chunky but clean 9-pixel run at 3x. The 7.4:1 luminance contrast against #172336 means the silhouette, not the hue, carries identity (silhouette-readability method: landmarks visible at the target size on the target background).
pixel_art_reasoning.stroke_and_step_construction: Both arms are exact 45-degree diagonals, so each contour steps one pixel per row with uniform run lengths (edge-rhythm method: a straight diagonal keeps a repeating step pattern; there are no detour pixels to correct). Nearest 3x enlargement reproduces every logical pixel as a uniform 3x3 block with no new colours (integer-presentation check), which I confirmed on view.2.
pixel_art_reasoning.silhouette_and_meaning: The check mark is the conventional completion sign. The 1:2 arm ratio makes it unmistakably a check rather than a V or a chevron, and the vertex at (6,12) places the long arm rising to the upper right, the reading direction for 'done'. The asymmetry the owner requires is realized here through arm length; the brief would also accept asymmetry through angle, thickness or position, so this construction is a choice, not the rule. The Start triangle (filled right-pointing, 10x12 in a 16 viewBox) is a different silhouette class; nothing about the check resembles pause bars, a loop or an X.
pixel_art_reasoning.ui_icon_contrast_and_colour: The single flat #70b9ed matches the flat vector Start control, which is the only existing UI art, so the sample proposes 'flat accent glyphs on the dark panel' as the family treatment. For a UI status icon at this size, shading adds nothing and a dark outline would eat into the 29-pixel mark; a lighter highlight tone remains an option for later members if the family needs more differentiation.
pixel_art_reasoning.transparency: The exterior is alpha 0 with no fringe; the mark is a single component, so there is no ambiguity about subject versus matte. The contract permits partial alpha (alpha 'full'); the fixture happens to be binary, which is an observation, not compliance with a binary rule (alpha-contract method: keep alpha policy separate from palette membership).
pixel_art_reasoning.centring: The 11x9 bounding box cannot be centred exactly in a 16x16 cell; its centre is (8.5, 8.5) versus (8.0, 8.0), half a pixel right and down, and the mass centroid (8.5, 8.74) is lower because the long arm's weight sits upper-right while the vertex is low. Optically the mark sits a touch low-right; for a check glyph whose visual weight is in the rising arm this is acceptable and I would not move it. Centring is not an owner criterion.
pixel_art_reasoning.cluster_hygiene: One 4-connected component, no isolated pixels, tips taper deliberately to single pixels (semantic-clusters method: legitimate singletons are the tapered tips, not noise).

family_recommendations_proposals: Keep about 2 px perpendicular strokes (3-pixel runs on 45-degree diagonals, 2-pixel-wide verticals/horizontals) and a footprint near 11x9 to 12x12 inside 2-3 px margins so all four marks have similar visual weight.

Working: four frames of a rotating three- or four-segment arc; avoid any diagonal pair that could read as a check in a single frame; keep every frame's footprint inside the same box so the loop does not jitter.
Retry: a circular arrow with a clear gap and a 2-pixel arrowhead; its curve distinguishes it from the straight-armed check in grayscale.
Paused: two vertical 2-pixel bars with a 2-pixel gap, about 8-9 px tall; pure verticals separate it from the diagonal check, the curved Retry and the arc frames without colour.
Reserve a secondary tone (lighter blue or near-white) for an optional highlight only if the family needs it; keep the primary fill shared.
